correctness.rationale: Explicit expansion of both published forcing clauses reduces each nesting to a relation over triples. Products of upsets separate downward-closure inequivalence by principal upper sets; complements of principal downsets separate upward-closure inequivalence for the saturated universal relation. Both directions are proved for any nonempty poset; the finite O(n^7) algorithm follows from enumerating quantified relations. Direct independent semantic/relational comparisons cover all 2 and 67 monotone frames on one- and two-point chains and 95 monotone functional frames on the three-chain; finite tests are not the unrestricted proof.

The 2024 associative-binary-modality paper treats a different, raw-relational/classical setting. The novelty claim is the general paired operator-specific criterion, not previously examined two-chain counts. value.rationale: The 2026 motivating text leaves associative binary-modal semantics as a substantive structural issue. Exact iff criteria distinguish the existential and universal operations on every ordered ternary frame, identify why raw associativity of the original relation is unnecessarily strong while strict associativity of its saturation is necessary for the universal operator, and allow deterministic polynomial finite-frame validity recognition without enumerating valuations. This solves the natural fixed-frame correspondence question while explicitly leaving strong completeness open.
